html:
The Évian Accords were signed on 18 March 1962 by France and the Algerian provisional government, ending the Algerian War. Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962, 132 years to the day after the French took Algiers.

President Charles de Gaulle had come to see that France could not win. The accords set a ceasefire and a vote on independence, which passed almost unanimously, and promised rights to the European settlers and French use of bases and Saharan oil for some years.

The months around independence were chaotic. The settler terror group OAS bombed and killed, and almost all the pieds-noirs fled to France, as did many harkis, Algerians who had served France; many who stayed were killed. Ahmed Ben Bella became the first leader.
